review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

4:1.sourceText: Λοιπὸν οὖν, ἀδελφοί, ἐρωτῶμεν ὑμᾶς καὶ παρακαλοῦμεν ἐν Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ, ἵνα καθὼς παρελάβετε παρ’ ἡμῶν τὸ πῶς δεῖ ὑμᾶς περιπατεῖν καὶ ἀρέσκειν Θεῷ, καθὼς καὶ περιπατεῖτε, ἵνα περισσεύητε μᾶλλον.
4:1.targetText: As to the rest, then, brothers, we request, and call on you in the Lord Jesus, as you received from us how it is necessary for you to walk and to please God, that you may abound the more,

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness difference: the first proleptic ἵνα in N1904 is absent from TR and unexpressed by LSV. The later actual ἵνα before abound stays linked to the one English that.
Greek nominalizing article before how has no separate English word.
Source-witness difference: N1904 includes καθὼς καὶ περιπατεῖτε, even as you also are walking, which is absent in TR and LSV.

4:2.sourceText: οἴδατε γὰρ τίνας παραγγελίας ἐδώκαμεν ὑμῖν διὰ τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.
4:2.targetText: for you have known what commands we gave you through the Lord Jesus;

4:3.sourceText: Τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἁγιασμὸς ὑμῶν, ἀπέχεσθαι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τῆς πορνείας,
4:3.targetText: for this is the will of God—your sanctification: that you abstain from the whoredom,

groups.note: The infinitive ἀπέχεσθαι explains the content of sanctification; LSV renders the infinitival complement as a that-clause with the same abstaining predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

4:4.sourceText: εἰδέναι ἕκαστον ὑμῶν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σκεῦος κτᾶσθαι ἐν ἁγιασμῷ καὶ τιμῇ,
4:4.targetText: that each of you know to possess his own vessel in sanctification and honor,

groups.note: The infinitival instruction εἰδέναι is rendered as the clause that each of you know; that belongs to this English clausal restructuring, not to a separate Greek conjunction.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

4:5.sourceText: μὴ ἐν πάθει ἐπιθυμίας καθάπερ καὶ τὰ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ εἰδότα τὸν Θεόν,
4:5.targetText: not in the affection of desire, as also the nations that were not knowing God,

groups.note: The present participle εἰδότα is rendered were knowing in the English relative clause; the auxiliary were is part of that English verbal construction, not a separate Greek past-tense copula.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

4:6.sourceText: τὸ μὴ ὑπερβαίνειν καὶ πλεονεκτεῖν ἐν τῷ πράγματι τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, διότι ἔκδικος Κύριος περὶ πάντων τούτων, καθὼς καὶ προείπαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ διεμαρτυράμεθα.
4:6.targetText: that no one goes beyond and defrauds his brother in the matter, because the LORD [is] an avenger of all these, as we also spoke to you before and testified,

groups.note: The article introduces the explanatory infinitival clause τὸ μὴ ὑπερβαίνειν, rendered that no one goes beyond; that is its clause-marking function here, not a general lexical equation for τὸ.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an indefinite subject one when rendering the negative articular infinitive as that no one goes beyond; Greek has μή, not a separate μηδείς.
English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

4:7.targetText: for God did not call us to uncleanness, but in sanctification.

4:9.sourceText: Περὶ δὲ τῆς φιλαδελφίας οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε γράφειν ὑμῖν· αὐτοὶ γὰρ ὑμεῖς θεοδίδακτοί ἐστε εἰς τὸ ἀγαπᾶν ἀλλήλους·
4:9.targetText: And concerning the brotherly love, you have no need of [my] writing to you, for you yourselves are God-taught to love one another,

groups.note: The infinitival complement γράφειν after have no need is rendered of writing; of is part of the English complement construction, not a second Greek preposition.
The articular purpose/result infinitive εἰς τὸ ἀγαπᾶν is expressed as to love in the English construction.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed writer possessive supplied from context; no ἐμοῦ or other explicit my occurs with writing.

4:10.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ ποιεῖτε αὐτὸ εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Μακεδονίᾳ. Παρακαλοῦμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, περισσεύειν μᾶλλον,
4:10.targetText: for you do it also to all the brothers who [are] in all Macedonia; and we call on you, brothers, to abound still more,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative pronoun and copula to express the Greek prepositional modifier in all Macedonia; there is no separate relative or being participle in N1904 at this point.

4:11.sourceText: καὶ φιλοτιμεῖσθαι ἡσυχάζειν καὶ πράσσειν τὰ ἴδια καὶ ἐργάζεσθαι ταῖς χερσὶν ὑμῶν, καθὼς ὑμῖν παρηγγείλαμεν,
4:11.targetText: and to study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you,

groups.note: LSV study uses the older sense strive/be ambitious, corresponding to φιλοτιμεῖσθαι; it does not assert that this Greek verb denotes academic study.
The substantival neuter plural τὰ ἴδια means ones own affairs, rendered your own business. The whole idiom is linked; no isolated article is assigned to your or business.
The dative noun phrase ταῖς χερσίν is rendered with ... hands; with expresses its instrumental case relation and belongs to the whole noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV own hands follows TR ἰδίαις, absent from N1904. The genuine earlier τὰ ἴδια stays with your own business.

4:12.sourceText: ἵνα περιπατῆτε εὐσχημόνως πρὸς τοὺς ἔξω καὶ μηδενὸς χρείαν ἔχητε.
4:12.targetText: that you may walk properly to those outside, and may have lack of nothing.

4:13.sourceText: Οὐ θέλομεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, περὶ τῶν κοιμωμένων, ἵνα μὴ λυπῆσθε καθὼς καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ οἱ μὴ ἔχοντες ἐλπίδα.
4:13.targetText: And I do not wish you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning those who have fallen asleep, that you may not sorrow, as also the rest who have no hope,

groups.note: The wishing predicate is shared, but N1904 θέλομεν is first-person plural and TR/LSV θέλω/I wish is singular. The unmatched English I remains explicit rather than being falsely assigned to we.
N1904 has present middle κοιμωμένων, those sleeping; LSV have fallen asleep follows TR perfect κεκοιμημένων. The same sleeping metaphor is linked while the aspect-form difference is recorded.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness person difference: LSV I follows TR θέλω I wish, while N1904 θέλομεν is we wish; only the shared wishing verb is linked.

4:15.sourceText: Τοῦτο γὰρ ὑμῖν λέγομεν ἐν λόγῳ Κυρίου, ὅτι ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες οἱ περιλειπόμενοι εἰς τὴν παρουσίαν τοῦ Κυρίου οὐ μὴ φθάσωμεν τοὺς κοιμηθέντας·
4:15.targetText: for we say this to you in the word of the LORD, that we who are living—who remain over to the coming of the LORD—may not precede those asleep,

4:16.sourceText: ὅτι αὐτὸς ὁ Κύριος ἐν κελεύσματι, ἐν φωνῇ ἀρχαγγέλου καὶ ἐν σάλπιγγι Θεοῦ, καταβήσεται ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐν Χριστῷ ἀναστήσονται πρῶτον,
4:16.targetText: because the LORD Himself, with a shout, with the voice of a chief-messenger, and with the trumpet of God, will come down from Heaven, and the dead in Christ will rise first;

4:17.sourceText: ἔπειτα ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες οἱ περιλειπόμενοι ἅμα σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁρπαγησόμεθα ἐν νεφέλαις εἰς ἀπάντησιν τοῦ Κυρίου εἰς ἀέρα· καὶ οὕτως πάντοτε σὺν Κυρίῳ ἐσόμεθα.
4:17.targetText: then we who are living, who are remaining over, will be snatched up together with them in [the] clouds to meet the LORD in [the] air, and so we will always be with the LORD;

groups.note: The preposition plus action noun εἰς ἀπάντησιν, for a meeting, is rendered by the English verbal phrase to meet.

Greek εἰς ἀέρα expresses the destination into the air; LSV in [the] air expresses the location of that meeting. The whole phrase is linked with this directional/locative rendering difference recorded.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English article before clouds is supplied; Greek νεφέλαις is anarthrous.
